title: Host keeps resending a retained prepared Begin after its Engram grant has expired, so the session is never re-admitted until someone cancels the head
outcome: A retained prepared Begin whose grant is expired, or provably unusable, is discarded or refreshed with a fresh evaluate, without operator action, while preserving every exactly-once and possibly-sent-Begin safety guarantee. A session is never stuck retrying a Begin that can never succeed.
acceptance: A kept prepared Begin that is provably never sent (its pending marker names its grant) and whose grant has passed the expiry turn_evaluate reported is never re-sent: the host's next automatic admission attempt withdraws it and runs a fresh turn_evaluate, whose new grant and new Begin key admit the head without Resume or cancel; a test covers it.
Resume of such a head likewise re-admits it through a fresh turn_evaluate instead of re-preparing the expired Begin; a test covers it.

A prepared Begin that may have been sent (no pending marker: after a restart, in a Begin replay, or with a Begin request in flight) is never withdrawn or re-keyed because of its grant's age; it keeps replaying the exact Begin, and only an Engram refusal proving it never began leads to a fresh evaluate; a test covers a possibly-sent Begin past its expiry being resent unchanged.
A kept prepared Begin whose grant has not expired, or whose expiry is unknown, behaves exactly as before; no case delivers a prompt to the provider twice; tests cover both.
Focused tests covering the change and its new tests pass in the item's named worktree, and the full gate is green on the frozen input.
The review pair (Codex and Claude, read-only) has no outstanding Medium-or-higher finding on the frozen input.
